utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. The Trial Chamber is following up on what was discussed yesterday. We are informed that the translation into Serbo-Croat has not yet been completed. Is that the case, Mr. di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: I just don't know, if Your Honours please. The motion was filed late yesterday afternoon -- the annex and part of the motion was filed earlier in the afternoon and I understand that translation was started earlier in the afternoon. The actual motion itself wasn't filed until later in the afternoon, the actual motion as opposed to the annex. So I don't know what the situation is in respect of progress in that -- as far as that is concerned. I just can't tell the Chamber what stage it's reached. It's being done in the normal course of events, I understand through Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, so we can only wait. MR. DI FAZIO: I just don't know is the short answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, and like we said yesterday, it's important that the accused get it in their -- in the language they understand and they can give instructions to their lawyers. In the meantime, I just want to inform the -- unless there is something else, Mr. di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Anything from the Defence? I don't think there can be anything before the papers are completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we actually -- good morning, Your Honours. I'm sorry. We actually received the document just two minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber is aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just want to inform the parties that the Trial Chamber was informed by the Victims and Witnesses unit about the condition of Witness M after the proceedings when he gave evidence. During the proceedings, he was asked to look at some documents and read them and that affected his eyes. Apparently he has a problem of inflammation with his eyes, so whenever he's asked to read anything that causes pressure and he had to be taken to the doctor. So I'm asking the parties to see whether that can be avoided next time he comes to give evidence, ask him to read. It is better for counsel to read, if it's necessary, and then put the questions to the witness. So we have that problem with Witness M. And we also were advised by the Victims and Witnesses Unit on the problem of witnesses who, after the Court has risen are spoken to by anybody in the courtroom. In this case it was Defence counsels. In this proceedings and another proceeding, in another Trial Chamber, and I did say earlier on that when witnesses are sitting in their box, they are not supposed to be spoken to by anybody, and that all of us all the parties, including the accused are supposed to observe those conditions in the courtroom so that the witnesses are not unduly under pressure except when the trial proceedings start. We will adjourn now and see how the progress will be on getting the documents translated and served on the accused, and the Defence, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Excuse me, just wait. When we are informed that those documents have been duly served, then we can sit and see what can be done. Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, although I didn't speak about this topic with my client, but I will just raise the issue. I think that it would be appropriate, of course with the decision -- after the decision of this Trial Chamber, maybe our clients for this particular issue can waive their rights to be here during these procedural matters, these proceedings about procedural matters. They can be transferred in the -- we can follow the progress about the translation of the amended indictment, then we can go and make a conference with our clients. In the meantime we could see what's going on. I don't think that it's appropriate, although the conditions here within this Tribunal for them are more or less good for the detention but still, I mean, they should be maybe with their papers, documents, whatever, in order to be ready for our conference. That would be my suggestion, of course, if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the Trial Chamber has looked into that possibility but then the Trial Chamber can't tell when the documents will be ready. And the transport system is also fairly rigid because there are other accused being transported to and fro and the people responsible for transport may not be readily available should we sit again this morning, before 1.00, to have the accused back In case the proceedings will require their presence. But if you're saying that they are waiving their right whatever proceedings follow on today, that is fine. That's their choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just make a short conference with my colleagues and also with the clients so we can know exactly what the case will be? Because, frankly, I don't believe that we shall have any kind of proceedings, including the appearance of the witnesses so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. There will be no witness today because the Trial Chamber will not have decided on the application. What the Trial Chamber will be interested in after the translation, after the service, that is the stand of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Our position maybe it can facilitate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Let's not go ahead. Let's wait for the translation and let the accused wait in the cells in the Tribunal. For those lawyers who after the translation is there, can get instructions, whichever position -- stand they want to take and they will be ready to make their submissions all the better. Because we have this courtroom up to 1.00 today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Up to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Up to 1.00. We can only sit in the morning because the courtroom is occupied in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There is another trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, so we will adjourn for the time being and wait for the progress and then we will be able to reassemble before 1.00. The Court will rise. --- Break taken at 9.41 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber has been informed that the translated parts of the actual amendments have been served, so the Trial Chamber would like to find out from the Defence whether they are ready to make submissions now or they need time or what is their position.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the fact that we received the translations just after 12.00 and have not yet had a time to consult with our clients regarding the receipt or the proposed amendments, we need more time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How much time?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I really can't say. I'm told that by looking at the B/C/S version, my understanding is my co-counsels even in have a problem with some of the translations. They say it is incorrect. So I don't know how to gauge how much time because I don't read the language and I don't know how significant the problems are. So I don't know if one of my co-counsel wants to address that or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Would it be all right if the Trial Chamber suggested to the Defence that they should put in a written response by Tuesday at 12.00?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We were going to ask leave to file something in writing because we thought it would be helpful to the Court so that sounds like a good idea. We accept that proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. To reply to this application for leave and to all the matters that have been raised by -- if you can file the written response by Tuesday, 12.00, and when I say Tuesday, I mean Tuesday, the 11th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That sounds good, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And also, if I may, Your Honour, since we are in the -- this kind of, I would say preparatory phase, it came to my attention that I'm reading the Prosecution motion for leave to amend the indictment, and in particular, I'm referring to annex A, the paragraph 14, and then the line actually the chapter E. The Expression, "the wanton and extensive destruction" is one term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just hold on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, so this is the annex A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 14. It's actually the second page of the Annex A and I'm referring to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Proposed amendment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Chapter e.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 14(e), "the wanton and extensive destruction," I mean I just need a clarification from the Prosecution but let me give my submission. So "the wanton and extensive destruction," term, is also in the paragraph 15, the subparagraph f, "the wanton and extensive destruction." And then we are going to paragraph 16, or rather 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 17(e), without "wanton". It's only "destruction". And also in paragraph 18(f) also just "destruction". So there is inconsistency between these terms, so maybe our friends can clarify that. Since we are in this phase maybe we can also do something on that matter. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because it entirely depends on how the Prosecution are going to present their case. Are there any comments on what Mr. Pantelic has said? MR. DI FAZIO: First of all, I don't think it's a matter of great significance, but I'm grateful to -- sorry, would Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: It's -- as I said, I don't consider it to be a matter of any great significance and, in fact, I'm grateful to Mr. Pantelic for pointing that out to us. I hadn't picked that up and we'll rectify that. Let me say this: I foreshadow a further brief application to rectify that mistake and bring it into line, and restore consistency in those paragraphs in due course but I don't think that's a matter that should trouble the Defence. It's not -- it's the least of chair concerns at the moment, given the substantial nature of the other application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but it does -- because when you talk of wanton and extensive -- wanton denotes knowledge and intention, all right? And when you simply -- you leave it out and deal with destruction only, the level of evidence, especially on the mens rea becomes different and sometimes one may argue that if you just put destruction is it absolute liability? MR. DI FAZIO: I see. I take your point. I'm not suggesting that the word is -- has no significance. I appreciate that. However, I would seek time to consider the matter and consider the effect of the adjective "wanton" on the rest of the phraseology and I foreshadow an application to restore harmony throughout those paragraphs either by the deletion of the word or by its inclusion in the missing paragraphs. And I think my learned friends from the defence now stand warned that there will be a brief application to fix that issue up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio, there is also the term "extensive" which is left out in the same paragraphs as Mr. Pantelic raised, so it's not just "wanton" but it's also "extensive" which clearly raises an issue in and of itself as well. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Because in those paragraphs that Mr. Pantelic raised, it simply says "the destruction, plundering and looting." MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Once again I'm grateful to Your Honour for pointing that out. That, of course, may depend upon the use of that word, may depend upon the class of property being attacked and destroyed and the extent of it; so therefore, that word may be of even greater significance and I'll make sure that that is also attended to in our further application to bring harmonisation to the wording of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Perhaps another thing that may require harmonisation or you may want to consider harmonisation, if at all, would be a number of phrases used say if you go back to the original charges, charge 13, sorry, paragraph 13, count 1, you have a number of mens rea, different mens rea n line 4, "planned, instigated, ordered, committed, otherwise aided and abetted." And then in paragraph 15 you have got the words "committed and aided and abetted." You've just got those two mens rea with the conjunctive. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Then you have at paragraph 19, you've got then the -- if you go back to paragraph 13, "planned, instigated, ordered otherwise aided and abetted the planning," then it goes into the other paragraphs as well. MR. DI FAZIO: I think those matters -- I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you want to explain that. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, well, I think those matters are attended to in the fresh -- in our application but I will also cast my eye again over those particular phrases that Your Honour has raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think this was discussed. It's only that I think Judge Singh was looking at the other part of the indictment because we have Annex B. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Is there any other matter that the Chamber wishes to raise on the wording of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think not. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would only like to say briefly a word about one detail I've noticed since we've got the B/C/S version of this annex. I have noticed namely that in Article 40 of the English version, the highlighted part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean paragraph 40?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 40, 4-0.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor stated in his submission that the parts which were added are highlighted in bold. And literally, it says in the English version, "acting in concert together and," [In English] "Crisis Staff" is not bolded. [Interpretation] In the B/C/S version also in bold, it says, "Acting in concert with," but then the words "with others in the Crisis Staff" is added -- are added. And before that, "And others" does not exist in the English version. Since every word carries a certain meaning, perhaps the translator wished to further explain this wording, but it is up to the Prosecutor in my view to explain the meaning of every addition to the indictment that he is proposing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the same section is highlighted in bold but one word is added in the B/C/S version, that is "in concert with," which does not feature in the English version. I am saying actually that we need to make a careful comparison of the two versions after a consultation with our clients. That is all, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps Mr. di Fazio can clarify paragraph 40. Is there any amendment to paragraph 40? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. And you can see that it's highlighted in our annex A. The problem that my learned friend refers to is really a problem of translation, isn't it? And one that I can't really assist with. Might I respectfully suggest and with the approval of the Chamber, perhaps they consult with the interpreters on this and see if they can sort the matter out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it's a problem with interpretation. MR. DI FAZIO: If that's suitable with the Chamber and if they inform us what their consultations with the interpreters produce, then I would be happy for them to speak to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you read 40? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: With the amendment? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I will, into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm now reading from Annex A of the Prosecution's motion for leave to amend the indictment, paragraph 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Slowly. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, Your Honour. I will endeavour to slow down. "Paragraph 40, from approximately 1st September 1991 through 31st December 1993, Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric, acting in concert together and with various individuals on the Serb Crisis Staff and other political, municipal and administrative bodies, the police force and the army, committed, planned, instigated, ordered or otherwise aided and abetted a campaign of persecutions for the common purpose of ridding the Bosanski Samac and Odzak municipalities of all non-Serbs and in furtherance of the campaign committed other serious violations of international humanitarian law directed against the Bosnian Croat, Bosnian Muslim and other non-Serb civilians residing in the Bosanski Samac and Odzak municipalities in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any other matters from the Prosecution? I know that the witness is not here. We have tomorrow. Unless the Prosecution have evidence which does not touch on the matters on the motion, it's up to you to decide. MR. DI FAZIO: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Whether you feel in the circumstances of these amendments that are still in process. MR. DI FAZIO: My preference would be to proceed. I have stated that now -- may I very briefly confer with my colleagues on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, the position of the Prosecution is that we would like to try and get as much evidence completed as possible. It's easy for me, I think, because they are quite separate and discrete topics, the evidence relating to the destruction to the religious institutions. It's easy for me to continue on with the other topics and hopefully get as far as I can with him. It's inevitable that he will have to come back next year and so I can finish the topic then once -- if it's appropriate, given whatever ruling eventuates. So, yes, my preference is to go ahead as far as I can tomorrow with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Provided you remember that he should not be asked to read any document. MR. DI FAZIO: I think I can deal -- I do have a last document but I think I can deal with that by simply reading the relevant portions that is I'm interested in into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yourself. MR. DI FAZIO: So I can save him from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the proceedings will continue tomorrow morning at 0930 hours. The Court will rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday the 7th day of December, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.52 p.m.,
